text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD: inference pool 'prod-gpu' reporting sustained queue growth; autoscaler failing to provision GPUs (zone capacity errors). Multiple nodes showing kernel Xid resets and driver OOMs. Paging on-call. thread_ts=4139876543

maya: taking pager. seeing significant 5xx spike on embed-heavy routes, router queue length doubling in ~8m.

junaid: autoscaler log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-15T21:12:04Z AUTOSCALE createInstances -> failed: ZoneCapacityUnavailable: requested 32 GPUs; available 0 in us-west1-b
2026-03-15T21:12:14Z AUTOSCALE retry -> throttled by provider
```

anika: kernel logs show repeated Xid 31 and Xid 13 across several nodes, followed by driver restart. Memory accounting looks weird; per-process GPU memory spike before reset.

trent: ops note: our reserved-dedicated pools in us-east have spare GPUs. Propose immediate traffic siphon there to stop queue growth while we triage. We'll accept some latency delta.

ops-runner: I'll update routing policy to send 50% to dedicated-east. Command we'll use: 
```
redwoodctl routes set inference --pool=prod-gpu --fallback=dedicated-east --fallback-weight=0.5
```

leah: starting customer impact triage. Early numbers: 18% increase in 5xx for hosted tenants, top-10 customers hit heavier. CS prep message and targeted outreach.

maya: also cordon flapping nodes to avoid scheduler placing work there. List from monitoring: gpu-node-w1-07, gpu-node-w1-09, gpu-node-w1-14. Trent/carl (ops) can you drain them?

trent: draining gpu-node-w1-07 now. note: one pod stuck on ephemeral volume; will force-delete if needed.

junaid: quick check on recent infra changes: a driver rollout (nv-driver-526.10) went to prod us-west yesterday evening. That's correlated with onset of Xid patterns. Rolling back driver on a canary to validate.

anika: ran stress repro on staging with nv-driver-526.10 and saw memory leak after ~5-10m under sustained attention workloads. Reproduced Xid 31. Rolling back to nv-driver-521.12 on canary stops the fault.

ops-runner: routing change applied. Traffic now 50% to dedicated-east. Queue length on prod-gpu dropped ~22% in 4m, 5xxs trending down. Latency +80-120ms for some regions.

maya: good. Action items: 1) keep fallback routing, 2) cordon+drain noisy nodes, 3) deploy driver rollback to flapping nodes as canary passes, 4) open provider quota request for more GPUs and cross-zone capacity, 5) CS notify impacted customers. Assign: @ops-runner routing, @trent draining, @anika driver rollback, @junaid provider contact, @leah customer comms.

junaid: opened cloud ticket CP-11555 asking for transient capacity bump and confirmation of regional availability. Provided incident context. Provider ETA unknown.

anika: canary rollback complete; no Xid seen in 12m on canary under load. Planning staged rollback at +3 nodes/minute with 5m observation windows.

trent: drained 3 nodes so far; one node forced due to stuck disk claim. Marked for reprovision.

ops-runner: ramping fallback to 70% while we rollback drivers. Queue and 5xxs continue to decline.

maya: note on autoscaler: because our autoscaler prefers same zone (us-west1-b) and quota is 0, it kept hammering the provider and failing. We need immediate cross-zone fallback in autoscaler logic so future incidents don't rely on single zone capacity. @junaid add to postmortem/resilience thread.

junaid: noted. I'll add autoscaler fallback task and include telemetry hooks so we can detect provider ZoneCapacityUnavailable and immediately switch pool weights.

anika: rollback progress: 9/12 noisy nodes completed; three still in progress. So far stable after rollback. One node needed full reimage due to corrupted driver state; reprovision in progress.

leah: customer-impact update: incident peak caused 30-40% failures for a small subset of enterprise customers for ~10-15m. Most customers saw degraded latency rather than full failure. CS sending targeted note and offering credits if SLA thresholds met.

incident-bot: NOTE: scheduled handoff in 30 minutes to junaid. Please ensure runbook & commands included in handoff.

maya: preparing handoff snippet: routing to dedicated-east at 70%, driver rollback to nv-driver-521.12 underway on flapping nodes, cloud ticket CP-11555 open, cordons/drains performed on nodes [gpu-node-w1-07,gpu-node-w1-09,gpu-node-w1-14,gpu-node-w1-19].

junaid: taking handoff. I'll continue monitoring autoscaler failures and coordinate with provider. If CP-11555 doesn't get capacity in 2h, we'll escalate to infra lead and consider longer-term cross-zone autoscaler change.

anika: final note: root-cause hypothesis: nv-driver-526.10 regression in memory accounting under high-concurrency attention workloads causing memory corruption -> Xid -> driver reset -> effective GPU capacity drop. Mitigations: rollback and add autoscaler cross-zone fallback + detect Xid spikes to autoreroute. Filing an RCA issue and infra ticket for autoscaler changes.

ops-runner: mitigation status: traffic rerouted (70% fallback), 10 noisy nodes rolled back and stabilized, 4 nodes cordoned and queued for reprovision. Provider quota still pending. 5xxs down to near-normal baseline.

leah: incident severity: medium. CS outreach in progress. Will update when provider responds to CP-11555.

maya: thanks team. Postmortem owners: anika (driver regression), junaid (autoscaler/resilience/quota), ops-runner (routing and runbook). Schedule 1h postmortem in 24h. Closing pager to junaid.

incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated (degraded service). Pager transferred to junaid. Keep thread updated with provider ticket and any Xid recurrence.

junaid: acknowledged. Monitoring for further Xid or autoscale events. Will update thread every 30m or on major changes.
